About.title: About us
About.intro: WWF Crotone is the local section of WWF Italia ETS, active in the Crotone province for biodiversity conservation, sea turtle protection and environmental education.
About.wwfCrotoneBody: The local section operates in the Crotone territory with conservation projects, summer volunteer camps, environmental education and awareness campaigns. It collaborates with institutions, schools and other third-sector organisations.
About.tartamarBody: TARTAMar Calabria is WWF Italia's regional project to monitor and protect the nesting sites of the Caretta caretta sea turtle along the Calabrian coast. Calabria is the second Italian region by number of nests, just behind Sicily. The project involves constant beach monitoring, search for nesting tracks, securing nests and data collection, using drones and Totò, our turtle dog (specialised canine unit) to locate nests.
About.crasTitle: Collaboration with the CRAS of Catanzaro
About.crasBody: WWF Crotone works with the C.R.A.S. (Wild Animal Recovery Center) of Catanzaro for the recovery, stabilisation and rehabilitation of wildlife in difficulty. Volunteers provide operational support during first-aid activities.
About.celaTitle: The C.E.L.A. — Center for Education on Legality and the Environment
About.celaBody: Volunteers stay at the C.E.L.A., a property confiscated from the mafia in San Leonardo di Cutro and granted on loan to WWF Crotone. The facility has a kitchen, common room, outdoor dining area, garden and dormitory rooms with bunk beds and shared bathroom. The beach is about 200 metres away. The C.E.L.A. is a concrete symbol of legality and rebirth: a property returned to the community, now a place of education, sharing and respect for the environment.
About.vergariBody: One of the natural jewels of the Crotone territory is the Vergari Regional Nature Reserve, destination of a guided excursion during the camp.
About.crtmTitle: CRTM Capo Rizzuto — Marine Turtle Recovery Center
About.crtmBody: The CRTM (Centro Recupero Tartarughe Marine) of Capo Rizzuto is a national reference point for the care and rehabilitation of injured or distressed Caretta caretta sea turtles. Managed by WWF Crotone under an agreement with the Marine Protected Area, the centre welcomes dozens of specimens every year from the Calabrian and Ionian coasts. Camp volunteers actively participate in tank maintenance, feeding, basic veterinary care and preparation for release back into the sea. The CRTM also carries out scientific research on sea turtle biology and ecology, contributing to national and international conservation programmes.
About.aquariumBody: The Aquarium CEAM of Crotone is a facility dedicated to the education about the marine fauna of the Ionian Sea, managed with passion and enthusiasm by WWF Crotone volunteers. Reopened after years of abandonment, it hosts several tanks with the main species of local marine fauna and four tanks dedicated to the care of sea turtles from the Capo Rizzuto CRTM. The aquarium represents a fundamental educational stop during the camp: volunteers deepen their knowledge of Mediterranean species, marine biology and first aid techniques for turtles in difficulty, becoming guides themselves for visitors and school groups.
About.mapBody: The main places where the camp activities take place: C.E.L.A. (accommodation), Capo Rizzuto Marine Protected Area (monitoring beach and CRTM), the Vergari Nature Reserve and the city of Crotone.

Activities.title: Camp activities
Activities.intro: Each week combines core conservation activities, secondary cultural activities and training moments.
mainList: Search for Caretta caretta nests, protection and support during hatching
Aquarium maintenance and management of the Capo Rizzuto Marine Turtle Recovery Center (CRTM)
Cleanup of beaches of particular naturalistic interest in the Capo Rizzuto MPA
Recovery and first aid of wildlife in collaboration with the CRAS of Catanzaro
Lesson on organised crime, legality and environment
Activities.secondaryIntro: Cultural and excursion activities take place compatibly with the camp's operational needs and the progress of the core activities.
secondaryList: Excursion to the Vergari Regional Nature Reserve (KR)
Visit to the Capocolonna Archaeological Park and Museum (extra booking)
Visit to Le Castella (Capo Rizzuto island), with optional extra visit to the Aragonese Castle of Le Castella
Environmental education on the beaches of the MPA (Marine Protected Area)
Activities.monitoringBody: Territory monitoring is carried out daily together with WWF operators, in the early hours of the morning. Turtle emergence tracks are intercepted before bathers arrive: human footsteps quickly erase the marks in the sand. Identified nests are monitored over time, until hatching, with possible night surveillance to ensure their protection. Alongside the operators works Totò, our turtle dog (canine unit) trained to search for Caretta caretta nests.
Activities.tartamarBody: TARTAMar Calabria is WWF Italia's regional project to monitor and protect the nesting sites of the Caretta caretta sea turtle along the Calabrian coast. Calabria is the second Italian region by number of nests, just behind Sicily. The project involves constant beach monitoring, search for nesting tracks, securing nests and data collection, using drones and Totò, our turtle dog (specialised canine unit) to locate nests.
Activities.eventsIntro: During the camp, volunteers can take part in the major WWF Italia national events — opportunities for awareness and active citizenship that involve millions of people across Italy.
Activities.earthHourBody: Earth Hour is WWF's global event that every year, on the last Saturday of March, invites citizens, institutions and businesses to symbolically switch off their lights for one hour. Born in Sydney in 2007, it has become the largest global mobilisation for the climate. During the March camp, volunteers participate in the initiative with a candlelit evening at the C.E.L.A., followed by a night walk on the beach to listen to the sounds of nature.
Activities.urbanNatureBody: Urban Nature is the WWF initiative dedicated to urban biodiversity: a day to rediscover nature in cities, parks and green spaces, with free events across Italy. Camp volunteers can take part as nature guides in local activities organised by WWF Crotone, bringing the experience gained at camp to schools and neighbourhoods throughout the province.
Activities.primaveraOasiBody: Primavera delle Oasi is the WWF annual festival that opens the Oases and nature reserves to guided visits, workshops and family activities. During the May camp, volunteers participate in the extraordinary opening of local protected areas, accompanying visitors to discover the biodiversity of the territory.
Activities.trainingIntro: The camp is recognised as a formative experience and can be integrated into institutional training, internship and orientation programmes.
Activities.internshipBody: Agreements with the main Italian universities (University of Calabria, Magna Graecia University of Catanzaro, University of Bologna, La Sapienza Rome, University of Padua, Polytechnic of Turin and others) allow the camp to be carried out as a curricular or extracurricular internship, with ECTS credits recognition. Postgraduate and professionalising internships are also available for biologists, naturalists, environmental scientists, biological sciences and related disciplines. For PhD students, the camp offers field research and data collection opportunities within the TARTAMar project and the Capo Rizzuto MPA monitoring.
Activities.coursesBody: The camp is accredited as a formative activity for the release of professional training credits for environmental guides, nature guides, environmental educators, green operators and similar roles. In collaboration with accredited training bodies, specific modules are organised on: wildlife monitoring, protected area management, environmental education, scientific communication and animal first aid. The courses are open both to camp volunteers and to external interested parties.
Activities.pctoBody: The camp is affiliated with Italian upper secondary schools as a PCTO activity (formerly Alternanza Scuola-Lavoro), with a certifiable hour count from 40 to 80 hours per week. High school students can carry out the camp as part of their orientation pathway, acquiring transversal competences in active citizenship, environmental sustainability, teamwork and communication. At the end of the camp, a certificate of participation is issued, valid for the student's PCTO portfolio.

Faq.title: Frequently asked questions
Faq.intro: Everything you need to know before signing up for the WWF Crotone volunteer camps. Use the search to find what you need instantly.
Faq.noResultsBody: We couldn't find an answer for "{query}". Try another keyword or get in touch with us directly.
Faq.contactBody: Drop us a line and we'll get back to you as soon as we can. For sign-ups please use the dedicated booking form.

generale.a: We are the local branch of WWF Italia ETS, active in the province of Crotone. We protect Caretta caretta sea turtles, run the CRTM rescue centre in Capo Rizzuto, lead environmental education and support wildlife recovery together with the CRAS in Catanzaro.

generale.q: Why is the camp called "Legality, Environment and Biodiversity"?
generale.a: Because it was born from the need to protect the Crotone province — home to the Capo Rizzuto Marine Protected Area (the second largest in Europe), the Vergari Nature Reserve and the San Leonardo di Cutro SCI — and because it takes place at the C.E.L.A., an asset confiscated from organised crime and given back to the community.

generale.q: What's the difference between a WWF member and a non-member?
generale.a: The fee is €400 for WWF members and €430 for non-members. The WWF membership card is included in the fee and supports the association. If you're not a member yet, you receive the card when you arrive at camp.

generale.q: Can I join with no prior experience?
generale.a: Absolutely — no experience needed. When you arrive you'll take a short training course on sea turtles and monitoring techniques. We guide you step by step: 80% of the volunteers we host every summer are first-timers.

generale.q: Is the camp suitable for high-school students?
generale.a: Yes, it is. The camp is accredited as a PCTO activity (formerly Alternanza Scuola-Lavoro) with 40 to 80 certified hours per week. Minors need a signed parent or guardian consent form.

generale.q: Is the camp suitable for university students?
generale.a: Definitely. We have active agreements with Unical, Magna Graecia di Catanzaro, Bologna, La Sapienza, Padova and Politecnico di Torino. The camp is recognised as a curricular or extracurricular internship with CFU credits.

generale.q: Can I join the camp if I'm retired?
generale.a: Yes, the camp is open to all ages as long as you are in good health and able to follow the activities. We've hosted volunteers from 16 to 80. Just complete the health section of the booking form.

generale.q: Can I come with my family?
generale.a: Yes, the camp is open to families too. Groups of at least 5 people get a dedicated discount: write to wwfcrotone26@gmail.com for a tailored quote.

iscrizione.a: When a turn is full you can ask to be added to the waitlist. We email you as soon as a spot opens up or a new turn is confirmed. To join, write to wwfcrotone26@gmail.com with the turn number and your contact details.

iscrizione.q: Can I cancel my registration? Until when?
iscrizione.a: Yes, you can cancel at any time by emailing wwfcrotone26@gmail.com. If you cancel at least 14 days before the start of the camp we refund the full €100 deposit (minus any bank fees). After that we evaluate case by case.

iscrizione.q: What happens if I don't pay on time?
iscrizione.a: If we don't receive the balance within 7 days of the turn starting, the spot is released to the waitlist. If you're having trouble, please contact us before the deadline — we're flexible when you let us know in time.

iscrizione.q: Can I switch to a different turn after signing up?
iscrizione.a: Yes, you can move to another turn if there's availability. Email us at least 15 days before the original start date and we move you across at no extra cost.

iscrizione.q: Can I gift the camp to someone?
iscrizione.a: Yes — it's a gift we love to arrange. Fill in the booking form in the name of the recipient and note in the contact details that it's a gift. We'll send you a dedicated confirmation with payment instructions.

logistica.a: At the C.E.L.A. (Centre for Education in Lawfulness and the Environment), an asset confiscated from the mafia in San Leonardo di Cutro. Shared rooms with bunk beds, en-suite bathroom, hot water and air conditioning. Rooms sleep up to 8 people, with separate rooms for men and women.

logistica.q: Is there parking at the camp?
logistica.a: Yes, the C.E.L.A. has a free internal courtyard for volunteers' cars. The area is fenced and under video surveillance, but as in any shared space we recommend not leaving valuables in sight.
Of course — we actually recommend it if you can: it gives you more flexibility for moving around. Select "Own car" as your arrival method in the form so we know you're self-sufficient.
We don't have a self-service laundry on site, but a hand-wash service for essential items is available. For special needs the coordinators can arrange an external laundry at modest prices.

logistica.q: How does the transfer service work?
logistica.a: For arrivals by plane at Lamezia Terme, by train or by bus, we arrange transfers with our own vehicles at €10 per leg. From Crotone-Sant'Anna airport and Crotone station the service is free if you let us know your schedule at least 7 days in advance.
Yes, when you arrive you receive the official camp T-shirt, the WWF membership card and an info pack with a map of the area, useful numbers and the weekly programme.
Yes, the C.E.L.A. is covered by free Wi-Fi for volunteers. The signal is strong in the common areas and a bit weaker in the rooms farthest from the router.

salute.a: Sleeping bag or sheets, towels, swimsuit, comfortable trekking shoes, sandals, hat, SPF 50+ sunscreen, a 1+ litre water bottle, head torch for night shifts, mosquito repellent and a light jacket for the evening. Check the full list on the "What to bring" page of the site.

salute.q: I have a chronic condition — can I take part?
salute.a: In most cases, yes. It's important to list any conditions and ongoing therapies in the health section of the booking form. For significant conditions we ask for a short medical certificate. If in doubt, write to us before signing up.

salute.q: I have allergies — what should I do?
salute.a: List every allergy (food, contact, insect sting) in the booking form. The kitchen is set up to handle allergies and intolerances, and a first-aid referent is always on site.

salute.q: Do I need a tetanus shot before coming?
salute.a: It's not mandatory but strongly recommended. During the week you may handle equipment, nets or animals. If you don't know your status, check with your local health authority and, if needed, get a booster at least two weeks before the camp.

salute.q: What if I get sick during the camp?
salute.a: A first-aid trained operator is always present on site. For situations requiring medical care, the Crotone hospital is about 20 minutes away. Every volunteer is covered by accident and liability insurance.

pagamento.a: By bank transfer to WWF Provincia di Crotone, IBAN IT30V0306909606100000107334. The €100 deposit secures your spot; the balance is due one week before the camp starts. Use the reference "name, surname, turn number".
Yes, instalments can be arranged for amounts over €600 (basically two or more turns). Write to wwfcrotone26@gmail.com and we'll agree on a plan before you sign up.

The WWF member rate (€400 instead of €430) is already a meaningful reduction. We don't apply extra student discounts, but the camp is PCTO- and internship-eligible, so it's often refundable through school or university funds.
Yes, groups of at least 5 people — families or friends — get a dedicated discount. Email wwfcrotone26@gmail.com for a tailored quote.

pagamento.q: How do the multi-week discounts work?
pagamento.a: If you sign up for multiple consecutive weeks we apply a progressive discount: 15% off the second week, 25% off the third and beyond. For example, 3 full-price weeks cost €1,290; with discounts, €1,118 — you save €172.

WWF Italia ETS is a Third Sector organisation: donations and membership contributions are deductible or detraibile under current Italian tax rules. Keep the payment receipt and ask your accountant when filing.

attivita.q: What do you do at camp?
attivita.a: The main activities are monitoring Caretta caretta nests on the beaches of the Capo Rizzuto Marine Protected Area, running the CRTM (Sea Turtle Rescue Centre) and the CEAM Aquarium, beach clean-ups, and first aid for wild animals with the CRAS in Catanzaro.

It's the WWF Italia regional project for monitoring and protecting Caretta caretta nests in Calabria — the second Italian region for number of nests after Sicily. It involves continuous beach monitoring, tracking nesting traces, securing nests and collecting data, also with drones and "Totò", the trained turtle-detection dog.

attivita.q: Why is the beach monitoring done at dawn?
attivita.a: Two reasons: to avoid the midday heat and, more importantly, to spot nesting tracks before beachgoers walk over them and erase the signs. Nests found are then monitored over time until hatching, with possible night-watch shifts to keep them safe.

attivita.q: Which excursions are included in the fee?
attivita.a: The excursion to the Vergari Regional Nature Reserve (Mesoraca) is included. The visit to the Capocolonna Archaeological Park and Museum and the entrance to the Aragonese Castle of Le Castella are part of the programme but require a small contribution for tickets, communicated on arrival.

attivita.q: What activities run when it rains?
attivita.a: When the weather is bad the beach work is replaced with indoor activities: maintenance of the Aquarium and CRTM tanks, training sessions, environmental education workshops, and cultural outings to the Capocolonna Museum or Le Castella.

attivita.q: Can I take part in all the excursions?
attivita.a: Yes, the excursions (Vergari Reserve, Capocolonna, Le Castella) are included in the fee. A few require booking and a small contribution for entrance fees; full details are shared when you arrive.

attivita.q: Is there a programme for children?
attivita.a: We don't have a dedicated programme for children, but families with kids from about 12 upward can join comfortably. For younger children consider their stamina: days start at dawn and are quite full-on.
Yes, when the sea allows we organise snorkelling sessions in the Capo Rizzuto marine reserve. We provide the basic kit (mask and snorkel), but bring your own mask for hygiene reasons.

attivita.q: Can I bring my own diving gear?
attivita.a: Of course, as long as it's certified and in good condition. For scuba dives you need a valid certification and a competitive medical certificate. We don't organise scuba dives at camp, but if you're certified we can involve you in monitoring activities.

dopo.a: Yes, at the end of the camp we issue a certificate of participation valid as PCTO for high schools and as a curricular or extracurricular internship for our partner universities. We suggest contacting your school or internship office in advance to activate the procedure.

dopo.q: Can I come back the following year?
dopo.a: Yes — and we love it when you do. Many volunteers return for several summers and become a stable part of our community. Returning volunteers get priority on turn selection and can apply as operators.

dopo.q: Can I become a WWF volunteer after the camp?
dopo.a: Yes, the camp is often the first step into active WWF volunteering. After the experience you can continue with the local activities of WWF Crotone, take part in our national events, or apply as an operator for the following seasons.

Yes, all former volunteers join the WhatsApp group and the "Alumni WWF Crotone" mailing list: we organise meet-ups and events, and keep you updated on initiatives, training opportunities and new camps.

dopo.q: Can I do the camp as a PCTO activity?
dopo.a: Yes, the camp is partnered with many high schools across Italy as a PCTO activity (formerly Alternanza Scuola-Lavoro). The certified hours range from 40 to 80 per week. Get in touch to activate the agreement with your school.

items.q: Can I join if I'm not a WWF member?
items.a: Yes. The fee is €430 for non-members, €400 for WWF members. The WWF membership card is included in the participation fee.

items.q: Can I join if I'm a minor?
items.a: Yes, minors can join with the consent of a parent or guardian and with a €20 surcharge for insurance. The consent form must be signed by the parent/guardian.
Sleeping bag or sheets, towels, swimsuit, comfortable shoes, hat, sunscreen, water bottle, torch for night shifts, repellent and comfortable clothes. A light jacket for the evening.
At the C.E.L.A. in shared rooms of up to 8 people with bunk beds and shared bathroom, air conditioning and hot water.
Yes: breakfast, lunch and dinner. Volunteers self-manage the kitchen with the help of the coordinators. Menus are available for vegetarians, vegans and celiacs.
Core activities are adapted to the weather. In case of bad weather, indoor training and Aquarium/CRTM maintenance activities are carried out.

items.q: How do I get to Crotone?
items.a: By plane: Crotone-Sant'Anna airport or Lamezia Terme. By train: Crotone or Botricello stations. By bus: Crotone bus station or Piazzale Nettuno. WWF Crotone offers a transfer service to/from the camp (€10 surcharge per leg from Lamezia). Arrivals and departures in the middle of the day are recommended.
Yes, the C.E.L.A. has Wi-Fi available for volunteers.

items.q: Can I come with my family?
items.a: Yes, the camp is open to families. Groups of at least 5 people get a discount.

Yes, at the end of the camp a certificate of participation is issued, valid as university training credits or as PCTO for secondary schools. We recommend contacting universities and schools for agreements or protocols.
By bank transfer to WWF Provincia di Crotone, IBAN IT30V0306909606100000107334. The €100 registration fee secures your spot; the balance is due one week before the camp starts.

items.q: Is there a cap on spots per turn?
items.a: Yes, each turn has a maximum capacity of 20 volunteers. We recommend booking early to secure your spot.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: Information notice on the processing of personal data pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Italian Legislative Decree 196/2003 (Privacy Code) as amended by Legislative Decree 101/2018, and the Italian Data Protection Authority's Provision No. 229/2014 (Cookies).

sections.p:
The Data Controller is WWF Crotone, local section of WWF Italia ETS, with operational headquarters at C.E.L.A. — Centro di Educazione alla Legalità e all'Ambiente, San Leonardo di Cutro (KR), Italy.

Contact details:
• Email: wwfcrotone26@gmail.com
• Phone: +39 351 3945109
• Website: https://wwfcrotone.it

WWF Italia ETS is a Third Sector entity registered with RUNTS, with registered office at Via Po 25/c, 00198 Rome, Italy, VAT IT02121111005, Fiscal Code 80078430586.

2.1 Data voluntarily provided by the user

Through the volunteer camp registration form we collect:
• Personal details: first name, last name, date of birth, age
• Contact details: email, phone number
• Health-related data: allergies, medications, swimming ability, tetanus vaccination status, self-assessed fitness level, dietary requirements
• Parent/guardian data (for minors): name, email, phone, consent
• Logistical data: chosen turn, arrival method, times, T-shirt size
• Payment data: payment status (registration fee and balance)

Through the newsletter form we collect:
• Email address
• Language preference (IT/EN)

2.2 Data collected automatically

During browsing we collect:
• IP address (for rate limiting and security)
• Browsing data (pages visited, times) via Plausible Analytics (only with consent)
• Theme preference (light/dark) saved in localStorage
• Language preference saved in a technical cookie

sections.h: 3. Purposes and legal basis of processing
sections.p:
3.1 Performance of a contract or pre-contractual measures (Art. 6.1.b GDPR)

Personal, contact, health, dietary and logistical data are necessary to:
• Manage registration and participation in volunteer camps
• Organise camp logistics (accommodation, meals, shifts)
• Ensure healthcare during the camp
• Issue participation certificates
• Communicate with volunteers for organisational purposes

3.2 Explicit consent (Art. 6.1.a and Art. 9.2.a GDPR)

With your explicit and freely revocable consent:
• We process health data exclusively to ensure your safety during the camp
• We send communications about future camps and WWF activities (marketing)
• We use your photographic and video images for documentation and promotion of activities
• We send the newsletter with activity updates

3.3 Legal obligations (Art. 6.1.c GDPR)

We retain data to comply with legal obligations (e.g. tax, insurance, anti-money laundering requirements).

3.4 Legitimate interest (Art. 6.1.f GDPR)

We process IP addresses for security purposes (rate limiting, abuse prevention) and retain technical logs to diagnose malfunctions.

sections.h: 4. Nature of data provision and consequences of refusal
sections.p:
Providing personal, contact, health and logistical data is mandatory to participate in the camps. Refusal makes it impossible to complete registration.

Providing data for marketing, newsletter and image use purposes is optional. Refusal does not affect participation in the camp.

Data is processed using IT and telematic tools, adopting appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security proportionate to the risk, pursuant to Art. 32 GDPR.

Specifically:
• Data in transit is protected with TLS encryption (HTTPS)
• Administrative account passwords are encrypted with bcrypt (cost factor 12)
• Access to the admin area is protected by JWT authentication with httpOnly, secure and sameSite strict tokens
• Uploaded files (receipts, images) are validated via magic bytes to prevent malicious uploads
• A rate limiting system is active to prevent abuse
• Database backups are encrypted and retained for a maximum of 30 days

Processing is carried out exclusively by authorised WWF Crotone personnel and, limited to health purposes, by first-aid staff present at the camp.

Personal data is accessible exclusively to:
• WWF Crotone camp managers (registration management, logistics)
• First-aid staff (exclusively for health data necessary for assistance)

Data is NOT transferred, sold or shared with third parties for commercial purposes.

We do not transfer personal data to non-EU countries. The site is hosted on servers located within the European Economic Area.

Third-party services used by the site:
• Plausible Analytics (EU, privacy-first, no personal data) — only with consent
• Open-Meteo (EU, weather API, no personal data sent)
• YouTube (video embed in nocookie mode, no cookies until interaction)
• OpenStreetMap (map embed, no personal data sent)

Data is retained for the time strictly necessary for the purposes for which it was collected:

• Camp registration data: 10 years from the end of the camp (regulatory, insurance and reporting obligations), unless earlier deletion is requested
• Health data: 10 years from the end of the camp (insurance obligations)
• Marketing and newsletter data: until consent is withdrawn or unsubscription
• Browsing data (technical logs): 30 days
• Rate limiting data (IP): 1 hour

Upon expiry of retention periods, data is irreversibly deleted or anonymised.

At any time you may exercise the following rights (Art. 15-22 GDPR):

• Right of access: know what data we process and obtain a copy
• Right to rectification: correct inaccurate or incomplete data
• Right to erasure (right to be forgotten): obtain deletion of data, subject to legal obligations
• Right to restriction: restrict processing in certain circumstances
• Right to data portability: receive data in a structured format and transfer it to another controller
• Right to object: object to processing based on legitimate interest
• Right to withdraw consent: withdraw consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of prior processing

To exercise your rights, write to: wwfcrotone26@gmail.com

We will respond within 30 days. If you believe the processing violates the GDPR, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Italian Data Protection Authority (www.garanteprivacy.it) or the supervisory authority of your country of residence.
We do not use automated decision-making processes or profiling that produce legal effects concerning the data subject, pursuant to Art. 22 GDPR.

This notice may be updated periodically to reflect regulatory or technical changes. The date of the last update is indicated at the top of the page. We encourage you to consult this page regularly. In case of substantial changes, we will inform you by email (if available) or with a visible notice on the site.

Cookie.title: Cookie Policy
Cookie.intro: This cookie policy describes the use of cookies and similar technologies on the WWF Crotone website, in compliance with the Italian Data Protection Authority's Provision No. 229/2014 and the Cookie Guidelines of 10 June 2021.
Cookie.whatAreBody: Cookies are small text files that websites save on your device during browsing. They are used to remember preferences, authenticate sessions, analyse traffic and improve the browsing experience. Cookies can be 'session' (deleted when the browser is closed) or 'persistent' (they remain for a defined period).
Cookie.necessaryBody: These cookies are essential for the operation of the site and do not require consent (Art. 122 of Italian Legislative Decree 196/2003).

necessaryTable.name: wwf_admin_session
necessaryTable.purpose: Maintains the authenticated session of the admin area. httpOnly, Secure, SameSite Strict.

necessaryTable.name: admin-lang
necessaryTable.purpose: Remembers the language chosen for the admin interface (IT/EN).

necessaryTable.name: theme (localStorage)
necessaryTable.purpose: Remembers the light/dark theme preference. Not a cookie but a localStorage entry.

necessaryTable.name: cookie-consent (localStorage)
necessaryTable.purpose: Records your cookie preferences. Not a cookie but a localStorage entry.

Cookie.analyticsBody: With your consent, we use Plausible Analytics, a privacy-first web analytics service hosted in the European Union. Plausible does NOT use profiling cookies, does NOT collect personal data, does NOT track users across different sites and does NOT create persistent profiles. The data collected is aggregated and anonymised. You can review Plausible's privacy policy at https://plausible.io/privacy.

analyticsTable.name: Plausible Analytics
analyticsTable.purpose: Anonymous statistics on pages visited (URL, referrer, device, country). No personal data.

Cookie.thirdPartyBody: The site may embed content from external platforms. These services may set their own cookies only when you interact with them:

thirdPartyTable.name: YouTube (nocookie)
thirdPartyTable.purpose: Videos are embedded in youtube-nocookie.com mode which does not set cookies until the user starts playback.

thirdPartyTable.name: OpenStreetMap
thirdPartyTable.purpose: The map on the contact page is embedded from OpenStreetMap, which does not use tracking cookies.

thirdPartyTable.name: Open-Meteo
thirdPartyTable.purpose: The weather widget queries the free Open-Meteo API without sending personal data.

Cookie.manageBody:
You can manage your cookie preferences at any time:

• From the cookie banner at the bottom of the page (on first access or after clearing browsing data)
• From your browser settings (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) to block or delete all cookies
• By visiting https://www.youronlinechoices.com/ to disable third-party profiling cookies

Disabling technical cookies may compromise the site's functionality (e.g. inability to maintain the admin session or language preference).
